title: The Kids Take the Climate Change Fight to Court

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听 The Reframers，这是一个专注于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带300件你最珍贵的私人物品去工作，你把一个DJ台变成了一个美丽的、有50年历史的文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的 The Reframers。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: As the movement to fight climate change gathers momentum, it has begun to make its way into a new battleground, courts.
sentences.zh: 随着打击气候变化的运动汇聚势头，它已经开始进入一个新的战场——法庭。

sentences.en: This week, a historic case has landed in a Montana courtroom where a group of young environmentalists is suing the state.
sentences.zh: 本周，蒙大拿州法院审理了一起具有历史意义的案件，一群年轻的环保主义者正在起诉该州。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague David Gillis explains why the case could be a turning point and what a win in Montana would mean for the future of the climate fight.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·吉利斯将解释为什么这个案子可能是一个转折点，以及在蒙大拿州的胜诉对气候斗争的未来意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Friday, June 16th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月16日，星期五。

sentences.en: David, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 大卫，欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So there's a trial happening right now in Montana, and it's a landmark trial involving climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以蒙大拿州现在正在进行一场审判，这是一场涉及气候变化的里程碑式的审判。

sentences.en: Why does this case matter?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个案子很重要？

sentences.en: It is a pretty remarkable moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常了不起的时刻。

sentences.en: I cover climate change, and I've written about international efforts to change policy across the globe, and a part of this is a really big move to get the courts involved.
sentences.zh: 我报道气候变化，我写过关于全球改变政策的国际努力的文章，而这其中一部分是让法院参与进来的真正重大举措。

sentences.en: People are suing states and federal governments and companies.
sentences.zh: 人们正在起诉各州、联邦政府和公司。

sentences.en: Most of those efforts have been proceeding slowly, but now this case in Montana has actually gone to trial,
sentences.zh: 这些努力大多进展缓慢，但现在蒙大拿州的这个案子实际上已经进入了审判阶段，

sentences.en: and it's the first time people have really had the chance to see if they can hold the government accountable for climate change.
sentences.zh: 这是人们真正有机会看到他们是否能让政府对气候变化负责的第一次。

sentences.en: It's called Held v.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“黑尔德诉”，

sentences.en: Montana.
sentences.zh: 蒙大拿州案。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me about this case, Held v.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么跟我讲讲这个案子，黑尔德诉

sentences.en: Montana.
sentences.zh: 蒙大拿州案。

sentences.en: Well, a few years ago, a group of 16 young people from the state of Montana sued the state for its role in supporting the fossil fuel industry and contributing to climate change.
sentences.zh: 嗯，几年前，蒙大拿州的16名年轻人起诉该州，指控其在支持化石燃料产业和加剧气候变化方面扮演了角色。

sentences.en: And I've been talking to these kids, and they tell a really vivid story about how the warming planet is actually negatively impacting their lives.
sentences.zh: 我一直在和这些孩子们交谈，他们讲述了一个非常生动的故事，关于变暖的地球实际上是如何对他们的生活产生负面影响的。

sentences.en: And I spent some time walking in the woods outside Glacier National Park with one of the plaintiffs, who was 15 at the time the case was filed, but is now 18,
sentences.zh: 我花了一些时间，和其中一位原告一起走在冰川国家公园外的树林里，起诉时他15岁，但现在已经18岁了，

sentences.en: and his name is Lander Bussey.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫兰德·巴西。

sentences.en: Yeah, so some of my earliest memories, especially with my dad, are really, really early mornings,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我的一些最早的记忆，尤其是和我爸爸在一起的记忆，真的是非常非常早的早晨，

sentences.en: getting up at like the break of dawn to get out onto the prairie or some new river that my dad and I were out to discover.
sentences.zh: 天蒙蒙亮就起床，去到我和爸爸要一起探索的大草原或某条新河流。

sentences.en: Lander and his brother grew up in the woods.
sentences.zh: 兰德和他的兄弟在树林里长大。

sentences.en: Things are, I remember the first time I ever caught a trout with my dad, being waist deep and chilling like 30 degree water.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的，我记得我和爸爸第一次钓到鳟鱼的那次，腰部浸在大概30度左右刺骨的水中。

sentences.en: Way bigger than the last one.
sentences.zh: 比上一个大多了。

sentences.en: I remember shooting my first deer, going on hiking trips, my first solo fishing trip with my friends.
sentences.zh: 我记得我射杀了自己的第一头鹿，去徒步旅行，和朋友们进行了我的第一次独自钓鱼之旅。

sentences.en: Fishing and hunting, and really having sort of this idyllic childhood in the mountains of Montana.
sentences.zh: 钓鱼和打猎，在蒙大拿州的山区里确实有这样一种田园诗般的童年。

sentences.en: We get over the hill, and sure enough, there's this huge, huge male grizzly who just turns his head around, stands up on his hindquarters, looks at us.
sentences.zh: 我们翻过山丘，果然，有一只非常非常大的成年灰熊刚好转过头，用后腿站立起来，看着我们。

sentences.en: And I was scared senseless.
sentences.zh: 我吓得魂飞魄散。

sentences.en: I'd never seen a bear in the wild by that point, and my dad just told me to enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 在那之前我从未在野外见过熊，我爸爸只是告诉我去欣赏它。

sentences.en: As scared as I was, I couldn't help but feel how surreal what I was experiencing was, and how special it was.
sentences.zh: 尽管我很害怕，但我还是忍不住感到我所经历的一切是多么超现实，又是多么特别。

sentences.en: Not many kids are ever going to get to see a grizzly bear, let alone in their wild native habitat, not behind bars.
sentences.zh: 没几个孩子能有机会看到灰熊，更不用说在它们野外的原生栖息地，而不是在铁栏杆后面了。

sentences.en: But they say that in recent years, it's become harder and harder to enjoy their own backyard.
sentences.zh: 但他们说，近年来，想要享受自己的后院变得越来越难了。

sentences.en: We had an instance where it was a naturally caused wildfire that was pouring over one of the hilltops,
sentences.zh: 我们曾遇到过一次自然引发的山火，它从山头漫溢过来，

sentences.en: and we could see these orange clouds projected up into the sky along with these plumes of smoke.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到这些橙色的云彩投射到天空中，伴随着滚滚浓烟。

sentences.en: A few years ago, wildfires came within sight of their home.
sentences.zh: 几年前，野火逼近了他们的家，肉眼可见。

sentences.en: I've had instances in both in middle school and in high school where we weren't allowed to go outside at all during the day because of smoke conditions.
sentences.zh: 无论是在初中还是高中，我都遇到过因为烟雾状况，全天根本不被允许出门的情况。

sentences.en: Wildfires are getting more intense.
sentences.zh: 野火变得越来越猛烈。

sentences.en: Smoke days are forcing them indoors.
sentences.zh: 烟雾天迫使他们待在室内。

sentences.en: They say the hiking trails that they use have been washed away by torrential downpours with more and more frequency as the weather gets more extreme.
sentences.zh: 他们说，随着天气变得越来越极端，他们经常使用的远足小径被越来越频繁的暴雨冲毁。

sentences.en: High water levels in the spring are usually an indication of really heavy runoff off the mountains, which really murks up the waters,
sentences.zh: 春季的高水位通常表明山上的径流量非常大，这会使水变得非常浑浊，

sentences.en: makes trout's feeding patterns way more sporadic and unaccessible, and often puts a dent in their populations as a result of that.
sentences.zh: 使得鳟鱼的觅食模式变得更加零星且难以接触，并因此常常对其种群数量造成打击。

sentences.en: And when I spoke to many of the plaintiffs, including Lander, they say that the landscape that they've come to cherish is changing in front of their eyes.
sentences.zh: 当我与许多原告（包括兰德）交谈时，他们说他们一直珍视的风景正在他们的眼前发生变化。

sentences.en: And it's not just aesthetics here.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是美学问题。

sentences.en: They talk about their health and the fact that their asthma is getting worse.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到了自己的健康，以及他们的哮喘正在恶化这一事实。

sentences.en: Some of them hunt and fish for food as part of their traditional cultures.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人为了食物而狩猎和钓鱼，这是他们传统文化的一部分。

sentences.en: They say that's getting harder to do.
sentences.zh: 他们说这变得越来越难做到了。

sentences.en: They say their property's being threatened by wildfires.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们的财产正受到野火的威胁。

sentences.en: And in their contention, that's the direct result of climate change.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这是气候变化的直接结果。

sentences.en: And they're asking their government to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 他们要求政府采取行动解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So their argument isn't just, I can't go outside and have a nice time enjoying nature.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的论点不仅仅是，我不能出门去享受大自然的美好时光。

sentences.en: They're actually saying, hey, this is messing up our lives, our health.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是在说，嘿，这正在搞砸我们的生活、我们的健康。

sentences.en: They're saying that it's actually changing fundamentally what it means to be a kid in Montana.
sentences.zh: 他们说这实际上从根本上改变了在蒙大拿州做一个孩子意味着什么。

sentences.en: So what's the actual legal argument here?
sentences.zh: 那么这里实际的法律论点是什么？

sentences.en: Because it's like, yeah, you know, it doesn't seem very fair, especially for kids who, of course, aren't at all responsible for climate change.
sentences.zh: 因为这就像是，是的，你知道，这似乎很不公平，特别是对那些当然根本不对气候变化负有责任的孩子们来说。

sentences.en: But how do you actually assign legal blame to your state government?
sentences.zh: 但是你究竟怎么把法律上的指责归咎于你的州政府呢？

sentences.en: Well, that was really the crux of the problem for these plaintiffs and plaintiffs in similar climate cases all around the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实是这些原告以及世界各地类似气候案件中原告的核心问题。

sentences.en: But it turns out there's one woman who's been working on that problem for a long time now.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，有一位女性长期以来一直在致力于解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Are we recording on our end?
sentences.zh: 我们这边在录音吗？

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 在录的。

sentences.en: We're good.
sentences.zh: 没问题了。

sentences.en: She's a nonprofit lawyer named Julia Olson.
sentences.zh: 她是一位名叫朱莉娅·奥尔森的非营利组织律师。

sentences.en: Hi, Julia.
sentences.zh: 嗨，朱莉娅。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: And she's really the architect of Held v.
sentences.zh: 她确实是黑尔德诉蒙大拿州案的架构师。

sentences.en: Montana.
sentences.zh: 蒙大拿州案。

sentences.en: Tell me about Julia Olson.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲朱莉娅·奥尔森。

sentences.en: Julia has been an environmental lawyer for a couple decades now.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅做环境律师已经有二十多年了。

sentences.en: And when I spoke to her, she described a specific moment when her work on climate change really came into focus for her.
sentences.zh: 当我和她交谈时，她描述了一个特定的时刻，当时她对气候变化的工作对她来说变得真正清晰起来。

sentences.en: It was the summer of 2006.
sentences.zh: 那是2006年的夏天。

sentences.en: It was very hot.
sentences.zh: 天气非常热。

sentences.en: And I was in Eugene, Oregon, where I live.
sentences.zh: 我在我居住的俄勒冈州尤金市。

sentences.en: She happened to be pregnant, and she went to the movies.
sentences.zh: 她当时恰好怀孕了，她去看了电影。

sentences.en: It's this old church that had been converted into a little theater, and An Inconvenient Truth was playing there.
sentences.zh: 这是一座被改造成小型剧场的旧教堂，里面正在放映《难以忽视的真相》。

sentences.en: An Inconvenient Truth.
sentences.zh: 《难以忽视的真相》。

sentences.en: That movie by former Vice President Al Gore.
sentences.zh: 前副总统阿尔·戈尔的那部电影。

sentences.en: And it changed her life.
sentences.zh: 它改变了她的人生。

sentences.en: We watched the film, and I just saw play out in front of me all the destruction that was already happening with climate change.
sentences.zh: 我们看了这部电影，我只是看到气候变化已经带来的所有破坏在我面前上演。

sentences.en: And really what was going to come next.
sentences.zh: 以及接下来究竟会发生什么。

sentences.en: And I cried through the whole film, practically.
sentences.zh: 几乎整部电影我都看哭了。

sentences.en: After that, I gave birth to my second son and really started thinking about, okay, what I'm doing right now is not making a dent in averting climate chaos.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我生下了我的第二个儿子，并真正开始思考，好吧，我现在正在做的事情对避免气候混乱起不到任何作用。

sentences.en: And we need the law to do better, and as lawyers, we have to do better to bring good cases before courts.
sentences.zh: 我们需要法律做得更好，作为律师，我们必须做得更好，把好的案件带到法庭上。

sentences.en: Julia realizes that she's not going to be able to have an impact on an issue like this by pursuing piecemeal cases here and there, as she had been doing.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅意识到，她无法通过像以前那样零敲碎打地处理个别案件来对这样的大问题产生影响。

sentences.en: Instead, she decides she is going to need a real overarching approach to take on what she is now very clear is the defining issue of her lifetime, as she believes.
sentences.zh: 相反，她决定她需要一个真正的总体方针来应对她现在非常清楚的、她所认为的她一生中具有决定性的问题。

sentences.en: What does she come up with?
sentences.zh: 她想出了什么？

sentences.en: Well, very soon after that, she learns about a legal theory.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那之后不久，她了解到了一个法律理论。

sentences.en: The public trust doctrine.
sentences.zh: 公众信托学说。

sentences.en: The public trust doctrine.
sentences.zh: 公众信托学说。

sentences.en: The idea goes that the government, whether it's the federal government or the state government, actually has a responsibility to take care of the natural resources,
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，政府，无论是联邦政府还是州政府，实际上都有责任照顾自然资源，

sentences.en: things like the land, the environment, and ensure that those are protected for current and future generations.
sentences.zh: 比如土地、环境，并确保这些资源为当今和未来的世代受到保护。

sentences.en: And the language in constitutions is often quite broad.
sentences.zh: 宪法中的语言通常相当宽泛。

sentences.en: The federal constitution guarantees the right to life, liberty, and property.
sentences.zh: 联邦宪法保障生命权、自由权和财产权。

sentences.en: It guarantees equal protection under the law.
sentences.zh: 它保障法律面前的平等保护。

sentences.en: And Julia sees an opening to apply this new theory of how she can prosecute climate cases with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅看到一个突破口，可以将这个关于她如何利用美国宪法以及各州宪法起诉气候案件的新理论应用起来。

sentences.en: constitution and state constitutions as well.
sentences.zh: 以及各州宪法。

sentences.en: But how is the government threatening those public natural resources?
sentences.zh: 但是政府是如何威胁这些公共自然资源的？

sentences.en: Like, how exactly is the government responsible for climate change and not, say, for example, a fossil fuel company?
sentences.zh: 比如，政府究竟如何对气候变化负责，而不是比如说，一家化石燃料公司？

sentences.en: Well, it's not the government itself that's producing the fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 嗯，生产化石燃料的并不是政府本身。

sentences.en: But Julia argues that the government plays a huge and important role in all sorts of other ways in supporting the industry overall.
sentences.zh: 但朱莉娅认为，政府在以各种其他方式支持整个产业方面发挥了巨大而重要的作用。

sentences.en: They permit all of the fossil fuel production and transportation and combustion that is happening.
sentences.zh: 他们批准了正在发生的所有化石燃料的生产、运输和燃烧。

sentences.en: The fossil fuel industry couldn't do what it does today without our governments.
sentences.zh: 如果没有我们的政府，化石燃料行业就不可能做到它今天所做的事情。

sentences.en: It just wouldn't be possible.
sentences.zh: 这是根本不可能的。

sentences.en: So, like, let's take fracking as an example.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如说，让我们以水力压裂法为例。

sentences.en: It was the Department of Energy of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 正是美国政府的能源部进行了研发，为化石燃料行业开发了这项技术。

sentences.en: government that did the research and development to develop that technology for the fossil fuel industry.
sentences.zh: 为了实现我们的化石燃料能源系统，投入了数以百亿计美元的补贴。

sentences.en: Billions and billions of dollars in subsidies go to make our fossil fuel energy system happen.
sentences.zh: 并且我们有追溯到20世纪60年代的证据表明，联邦政府知道，如果他们继续允许并促进化石燃料的燃烧，

sentences.en: And we have evidence going back to the 1960s where the federal government knew that if they continued to allow and promote the burning of fossil fuels,
sentences.zh: 那将导致灾难性的气候变化。

sentences.en: that it would cause catastrophic climate change.
sentences.zh: 那将导致灾难性的气候变化。

sentences.en: And she makes the argument that even with that knowledge, it has failed to change its ways.
sentences.zh: 她提出论点称，即使掌握了这些知识，它也未能改变做法。

sentences.en: So, her argument is that the government not only created an environment for fossil fuel industries to thrive, they knew that doing so would contribute to climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以，她的论点是，政府不仅为化石燃料行业的蓬勃发展创造了环境，他们还知道这样做会导致气候变化。

sentences.en: That's the case she's making.
sentences.zh: 这就是她正在提出的诉讼主张。

sentences.en: But, David, just to push back for a second, though, how fair is it to hold governments accountable for this?
sentences.zh: 但是，大卫，稍微反驳一下，让政府为此承担责任究竟有多公平？

sentences.en: Like, climate change is so complicated, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，气候变化太复杂了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, how do you zero in on the government in particular as being the cause of these effects when everything they did is just, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当他们所做的一切只是，你知道的，

sentences.en: basically capitalism in a way and making it possible for our economy to function?
sentences.zh: 基本上某种程度上的资本主义，并使我们的经济能够运转时，你如何把矛头精确指向政府，将其视为这些影响的根源呢？

sentences.en: It's a question that's right at the heart of the cases she's bringing.
sentences.zh: 这个问题正处于她所提出的诉讼的核心。

sentences.en: And I asked her this very question,
sentences.zh: 我问了她正是这个问题，

sentences.en: how do you make that leap from the government letting the world continue apace without completely blowing up the global economy to actually suggesting that they're doing something,
sentences.zh: 你如何实现这种跨越：从政府让世界继续快速发展而不彻底炸毁全球经济，到实际暗示他们正在做一些，

sentences.en: I don't know, nefarious or that is directly, to use your framing, in violation of the public trust?
sentences.zh: 我不知道，邪恶的事情，或者用你的框架来说，直接违反了公众信托？

sentences.en: I mean, doesn't the public trust also ensure the ability to go make money and go to the movies?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，公众信托难道不也保障了去赚钱和看电影的能力吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, David, so I'll push back there a bit.
sentences.zh: 是的，大卫，所以我在这里要反驳一下。

sentences.en: So, our cases are about the public truSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的案件是关于公众信托的。

sentences.en: They're also about constitutional rights.
sentences.zh: 它们也关乎宪法权利。

sentences.en: And she comes back to this issue that there are central rights that we have as citizens.
sentences.zh: 她回到了这个议题，即我们作为公民拥有核心权利。

sentences.en: And those rights are threatened right now.
sentences.zh: 而这些权利现在受到了威胁。

sentences.en: And when government takes actions that affirmatively threaten the lives of children, their homes, their bodies, their personal security,
sentences.zh: 当政府采取积极威胁儿童的生命、他们的家园、他们的身体、他们的个人安全以及他们在法律面前获得平等保护的权利的行动时，人们就可以诉诸法院并提出宪法诉讼。

sentences.en: and their rights of equal protection under the law, then people can go to court and bring constitutional claiMs.
sentences.zh: 并在法律面前获得平等保护的权利，那么人们就可以去法院提出宪法诉讼。

sentences.en: And so now it's time for the courts to get involved.
sentences.zh: 所以现在是法院介入的时候了。

sentences.en: Okay, so she lands on this argument.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以她得出了这个论点。

sentences.en: What does she do with it?
sentences.zh: 她用它来做什么？

sentences.en: So in 2010, Julia founds an organization called Our Children's Trust, which is a nonprofit law firm that starts to bring constitutional climate cases on behalf of children.
sentences.zh: 因此，在2010年，朱莉娅创立了一个名为“我们的儿童信托”的组织，这是一个非营利性律所，开始代表儿童提起宪法气候诉讼。

sentences.en: And she really decides to focus on children because, she says, they don't have the ability to vote, they don't have representation,
sentences.zh: 她确实决定把重点放在儿童身上，因为她说，他们没有投票权，没有代表权，

sentences.en: and they are going to be the ones that experience climate change most intensely in the generations ahead.
sentences.zh: 而且他们将是在未来几代人中最强烈地体验到气候变化的一群人。

sentences.en: And pretty quickly, Our Children's Trust goes on and files cases in all 50 states and sues the federal government as well.
sentences.zh: 很快，“我们的儿童信托”继续在所有50个州提起诉讼，并起诉了联邦政府。

sentences.en: How do they go?
sentences.zh: 进展如何？

sentences.en: Well, most of them don't get very far.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大多数都没有取得太大进展。

sentences.en: They face opposition in the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 他们在法庭上面临阻力。

sentences.en: Some of them are struck down.
sentences.zh: 其中一些被驳回了。

sentences.en: And so it's not looking great for a little bit there.
sentences.zh: 所以在那里的一段时间里，情况看起来不太妙。

sentences.en: But then they find a new approach.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们找到了新的方法。

sentences.en: And it has everything to do with the state of Montana specifically.
sentences.zh: 这与蒙大拿州本身的情况完全相关。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中度过七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星的背后有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 它们可能每年都是联盟里最好的团队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，帮助您理解世界，充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受 nytimes.com 上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: David, you just told us about the lawyer behind this lawsuit in Montana.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你刚刚给我们介绍了蒙大拿州这起诉讼背后的律师。

sentences.en: But what makes Montana the place where a case like this could go to trial?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么让蒙大拿州成为这种案件能够开庭审理的地方？

sentences.en: Well, the Montana state constitution actually has very specific language in it that guarantees
sentences.zh: 嗯，蒙大拿州宪法其实有非常具体的表述，它保证了

sentences.en: residents the right to a clean and healthful environment and says it's the responsibility
sentences.zh: 居民享有清洁和健康环境的权利，并表示

sentences.en: of the government and citizens to protect that pristine natural environment for present and future generations.
sentences.zh: 政府和公民有责任为现在和未来的代际保护这片原始的自然环境。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is not an implied right.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这不是一种隐含的权利。

sentences.en: It's actually right there in black and white, like plainly in the text of the state constitution.
sentences.zh: 它实际上就白纸黑字地写在那里，明明白白地印在州宪法的正文中。

sentences.en: Yeah, Julia had been making a sort of broader argument about the public trust and the responsibility of governments to take care of their people.
sentences.zh: 是的，朱莉此前提出了一个更广泛的论点，关于公众信任以及政府照顾其人民的责任。

sentences.en: But in Montana, she didn't need to do all this work interpreting other vague language.
sentences.zh: 但在蒙大拿州，她不需要做所有这些解释其他模糊语言的工作。

sentences.en: It was right there in the law.
sentences.zh: 它就写在法律里。

sentences.en: And in fact, there are several other states that already have similar language in their state constitutions.
sentences.zh: 事实上，还有其他几个州已经在其州宪法中有了类似的表述。

sentences.en: Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Pennsylvania, Hawaii, New York added similar language to its constitution last year.
sentences.zh: 马萨诸塞州、罗得岛州、宾夕法尼亚州、夏威夷州，纽约州去年也在其宪法中加入了类似表述。

sentences.en: And around the country, there are even other states that are trying to get similar language added even today.
sentences.zh: 在全国各地，甚至还有其他州在今天试图将类似的表述加入宪法。

sentences.en: And for Julia and her team, this language was really the key to unlocking a strategy that allowed them to get this case to trial.
sentences.zh: 对于朱莉和她的团队来说，这种表述确实是解开战略的关键，使他们能够将此案推上法庭。

sentences.en: So why did Montana have this in their state constitution?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么蒙大拿州的州宪法里会有这个？

sentences.en: Like, how did that happen?
sentences.zh: 比方说，这是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Well, here we need to rewind.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里我们需要倒回从前。

sentences.en: Back in the late 19th century, the mining industry became big business in Montana.
sentences.zh: 早在19世纪末，采矿业成为蒙大拿州的大生意。

sentences.en: And it started exerting its influence not only over the state's economy, but over the government as well.
sentences.zh: 它开始施加影响，不仅控制着该州的经济，还控制着政府。

sentences.en: One historian I talked to called Montana a corporate colony.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的一位历史学家称蒙大拿州为企业殖民地。

sentences.en: And when the Montana state constitution is actually first written, the language in it is almost entirely deferential to mining interests and to energy interests.
sentences.zh: 当蒙大拿州宪法最初撰写时，其中的表述几乎完全顺从于采矿业和能源利益。

sentences.en: I mean, corporate colony is a pretty strong phrase.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，企业殖民地是一个相当强烈的词。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then in the early 1970s, in the throes of that late 60s, early 70s environmental movement.
sentences.zh: 然后在20世纪70年代初，在60年代末、70年代初那场环保运动的狂热中。

sentences.en: Montana citizens came to the state capitol well aware of the issues and determined to write a new constitution to better serve the state for the 1970s and the years ahead.
sentences.zh: 蒙大拿州公民带着对问题的清醒认识来到州首府，决心撰写一部新宪法，以便在20世纪70年代及未来更好地服务该州。

sentences.en: Montana's actually hold a constitutional convention.
sentences.zh: 蒙大拿州实际上召开了一场制宪会议。

sentences.en: That we are actually representatives of the people of the fine state of Montana.
sentences.zh: 我们确实是蒙大拿州这个美好州的人民的代表。

sentences.en: So with that in mind, let's put ourselves to the task of creating the very best constitution that we can get.
sentences.zh: 因此，带着这一点，让我们着手制定我们能得到的最好的宪法。

sentences.en: They decide to rewrite their constitution.
sentences.zh: 他们决定重写他们的宪法。

sentences.en: Is not Montana our home?
sentences.zh: 蒙大拿难道不是我们的家吗？

sentences.en: Is not the world our home?
sentences.zh: 世界难道不是我们的家吗？

sentences.en: Should we not have the right to protect our homes by appropriate legal proceedings against those who would defile it?
sentences.zh: 我们难道不应该有权通过适当的法律程序，保护我们的家园不受那些玷污它的人的侵害吗？

sentences.en: And a big part of why they do that is to take back control of their state government from what they see as the undue excessive influence of the mining community and the fossil fuel industry.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做的很大一部分原因，是要从他们眼中采矿界和化石燃料行业过度的不当影响手中夺回对州政府的控制权。

sentences.en: So many of you shall be in favor of the motion to adjourn, sign an eye, say aye.
sentences.zh: 因此，赞成休会动议的请举手，赞成请说“赞成”。

sentences.en: Aye.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: Opposed, no.
sentences.zh: 反对的请说“反对”。

sentences.en: It's so ordered.
sentences.zh: 就这么决定了。

sentences.en: And that's when they add this language.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们加入这番表述的时候。

sentences.en: So when this language was added, it was really before there was a widespread acceptance and understanding of what was causing climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以，当加入这段表述时，那其实是在人们普遍接受和理解气候变化原因之前。

sentences.en: The language was added to the Montana constitution really in response to the mining industry and how much pollution there was in the state because of it.
sentences.zh: 在蒙大拿州宪法中加入这段表述，实际上是为了回应采矿业以及由此给该州带来的严重污染。

sentences.en: But the language was still pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 但这段表述仍然相当明确。

sentences.en: The government, it now said, had a responsibility to give its citizens a clean and healthful environment.
sentences.zh: 它现在规定，政府有责任为公民提供清洁和健康的环境。

sentences.en: But over the last few decades, Montana's fossil fuel production has soared.
sentences.zh: 但在过去几十年里，蒙大拿州的化石燃料产量飙升。

sentences.en: Montana is the nation's fifth largest producer of coal and the 12th largest producer of oil.
sentences.zh: 蒙大拿州是美国第五大煤炭生产国和第十二大石油生产国。

sentences.en: And the state's government has done a lot to support that development.
sentences.zh: 该州政府为支持这一开发做了大量工作。

sentences.en: And what kinds of supports, David?
sentences.zh: 大卫，那是什么支持？

sentences.en: Like the kind that Julia was talking about?
sentences.zh: 就像朱莉刚才谈到的那种吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Permits, subsidies.
sentences.zh: 许可证，补贴。

sentences.en: The state's Republican government is currently very, very pro-fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 该州的共和党政府目前非常非常支持化石燃料。

sentences.en: And in fact, they recently passed a law that bars the state's permitting board from considering climate and emissions when deciding whether to allow a new project to get built.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们最近通过了一项法律，禁止该州的许可委员会在决定是否允许新项目建设时考虑气候和排放问题。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Like it can't even take climate change into account at all.
sentences.zh: 就像它完全不能把气候变化考虑在内一样。

sentences.en: That just seems pretty crazy.
sentences.zh: 这听起来简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: That's just the kind of thing that the plaintiffs and Julia say is the problem with the way the state is operating right now.
sentences.zh: 这正是原告和朱莉所说的那种问题，也就是该州目前的运作方式存在的问题。

sentences.en: Okay, so I'm guessing that the state government in Montana does not love this lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我猜蒙大拿州政府一定很不乐意看到这起诉讼。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不乐意。

sentences.en: It has responded incredibly strongly to this.
sentences.zh: 它对此做出了极其强烈的反应。

sentences.en: And since 2020, when this case was filed, and it was actually a Democrat who was governor, the state has tried to fight it every step of the way.
sentences.zh: 自2020年提起这起诉讼（当时州长实际上是一名民主党人）以来，该州一直在各个环节试图与之抗争。

sentences.en: And what's the state's argument?
sentences.zh: 那么该州的论点是什么？

sentences.en: Like what's its defense against Julia's case?
sentences.zh: 比如它对朱莉的案件有什么辩护？

sentences.en: Well, we will see the defense play out at trial.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们将看到辩护在审判中展开。

sentences.en: But what the state is contending is that even if fossil fuels are contributing to climate change at large,
sentences.zh: 但该州主张的是，即使化石燃料总体上导致了气候变化，

sentences.en: it's almost impossible to say that the specific emissions caused by fossil fuels in Montana are specifically responsible for the effects that they are seeing in that state.
sentences.zh: 也几乎无法断言蒙大拿州化石燃料产生的具体排放直接导致了他们在该州所看到的种种影响。

sentences.en: And thus specifically responsible for the damages that the children say that they are incurring.
sentences.zh: 从而也就无法断言其直接导致了孩子们所说的他们正在遭受的损害。

sentences.en: So this is interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, on the one hand, we know that without a doubt, anytime you burn fossil fuels, it makes climate change worse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一方面，我们毫无疑问地知道，任何时候燃烧化石燃料都会加剧气候变化。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, you can't pin climate change on one single factory or one single mine or even one single state.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，你不能把气候变化归咎于某一个工厂、某一个矿井，甚至某一个州。

sentences.en: And this is one of the reasons why so many people are watching this case so closely.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么这么多人都在密切关注这起案件的原因之一。

sentences.en: You can't say that the emissions from one particular coal plant in Montana made a forest fire in Glacier National Park that much worse.
sentences.zh: 你不能说蒙大拿州某座特定的燃煤电厂排放的废气，让冰川国家公园的森林大火变得那么严重。

sentences.en: On the other hand, we know that all of this is adding up and warming our planets right now.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们知道这一切都在累积，并在当前让我们的地球变暖。

sentences.en: And critically, so far, the courts have not allowed that argument as a way to let the state off the hook here.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，到目前为止，法院并没有允许这种辩护成为让该州脱身的理由。

sentences.en: We're also going to see, at this trial, the real introduction of what's known as attribution science.
sentences.zh: 我们还将在这场审判中看到被称为归因科学的领域的真正引入。

sentences.en: That is, the growing body of scientific work that more compellingly and more specifically than has been possible, even as recently as a couple years ago, make direct connections.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这门不断发展的科学研究能够比哪怕就在几年前更具说服力、更具体地建立直接联系。

sentences.en: So what exactly do Julia and the kids want to change?
sentences.zh: 那么朱莉和孩子们到底想改变什么？

sentences.en: Like, if they win, what do they imagine will happen?
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果他们赢了，他们想象会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, they're not seeking money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们不寻求金钱赔偿。

sentences.en: And that's important because a lot of people are contending that these kids who have decided to be a part of this case are somehow like the puppets of environmental renegades.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为许多人一直在争辩说，这些决定参与此案的孩子在某种程度上就像是环保叛逆者的傀儡。

sentences.en: And the kids will say, like, we're not asking for anything that's going to benefit us specifically.
sentences.zh: 而孩子们会说，我们没有要求任何会让我们获得特殊利益的东西。

sentences.en: Instead, what they want is declaratory relief.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们想要的是宣告性济助。

sentences.en: They just want the state to acknowledge that the burning of fossil fuels in the state and the permitting and subsidizing of things like oil and coal and gas is making the climate crisis worse.
sentences.zh: 他们只希望州政府承认，在该州燃烧化石燃料以及对石油、煤炭和天然气等项目的许可和补贴，正在加剧气候危机。

sentences.en: More specifically, though, they are potentially going to seek changes in state law.
sentences.zh: 不过更具体地说，他们可能会寻求修改州法律。

sentences.en: Remember the law I mentioned earlier about how the state can no longer consider climate change when approving a major project?
sentences.zh: 还记得我前面提到的关于该州在批准重大项目时不再能考虑气候变化的法律吗？

sentences.en: That's the kind of thing that could potentially be repealed if the children and Julia win here.
sentences.zh: 如果孩子和朱莉在这里获胜，这类法律就有可能被废除。

sentences.en: And from a purely symbolic standpoint, it would be one of the first times that a state government is saying, yeah, we bear some responsibility here.
sentences.zh: 从纯粹的象征意义来看，这将是州政府首次表态：是的，我们在这里负有一定责任。

sentences.en: And that opens up a whole can of worms for what that means down the road, what it means for other states, and what kind of precedent it might set.
sentences.zh: 这打开了一个潘多拉的魔盒，意味着未来会怎样，对其他州意味着什么，以及它可能会树立什么样的先例。

sentences.en: And because, you know, the judge surely knows it would open that big can of worms, I wonder if it feels unlikely that Julia and these kids win.
sentences.zh: 鉴于法官肯定知道这会打开那个巨大的潘多拉魔盒，我想知道朱莉和这些孩子们获胜的可能性是否不大。

sentences.en: Yeah, it would be unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 是的，这将是史无前例的。

sentences.en: And it's something I asked Julia about.
sentences.zh: 这也是我向朱莉询问过的问题。

sentences.en: Do you have concerns that what you're trying to bite off here is just too big for any one court to chew on?
sentences.zh: 你是否担心你在这里试图咬下的东西，对任何一家法院来说都过于庞大而难以消化？

sentences.en: No, I don't have concerns.
sentences.zh: 不，我不担心。

sentences.en: And I sit here as a woman.
sentences.zh: 我作为一名女性坐在这里。

sentences.en: And if courts hadn't been willing to take on that big question of whether someone like me was entitled to the equal protection of the law, I mean,
sentences.zh: 如果法院当初不愿承担那个重大问题，即像我这样的人是否有权获得法律的平等保护，我的意思是，

sentences.en: my life would have been completely different growing up.
sentences.zh: 我成长过程中的生活将完全不同。

sentences.en: She placed this case in the context of other big social movements in our country's history, things like women's rights and civil rights.
sentences.zh: 她将这个案件置于我们国家历史上其他重大社会运动的背景下，比如女性权利和民权运动。

sentences.en: If courts hadn't been willing to reverse Plessy v.
sentences.zh: 如果法院当时不愿意推翻普莱西诉

sentences.en: Ferguson and say that segregation was unconstitutional, I wouldn't want to live in that kind of world.
sentences.zh: 弗格森案并宣布隔离是违宪的，我可不想生活在那种世界里。

sentences.en: Well, similarly, I don't think any of us wants to live in a world ravaged by climate change.
sentences.zh: 同样，我想我们谁也不想生活在一个饱受气候变化蹂躏的世界里。

sentences.en: And no politician gets to decide if our kids get to grow up in a safe climate.
sentences.zh: 没有任何政客可以决定我们的孩子是否能在安全的气候中成长。

sentences.en: That's a matter of life and liberties.
sentences.zh: 这是生命和自由的问题。

sentences.en: And it's up to our courts to judge whether we hold those rights and if our government is violating them.
sentences.zh: 我们的法院有责任裁决我们是否拥有这些权利，以及我们的政府是否在侵犯这些权利。

sentences.en: One of the reasons this case is so interesting is that behind it is an absolute avalanche of other cases that are making similar arguments in different ways and trying to hold not only governments accountable,
sentences.zh: 这个案件如此有趣的原因之一在于，它的背后是绝对海量的其他案件，它们正以不同的方式提出类似的主张，试图追究不仅是政府的责任，

sentences.en: but specific companies as well.
sentences.zh: 还有特定公司的责任。

sentences.en: And so this is not the last time we're going to be hearing about climate litigation.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝不是我们最后一次听到关于气候诉讼的消息。

sentences.en: These cases, after fits and starts and dismissals and appeals, finally made their way to trial.
sentences.zh: 这些案件在经历了一波三折、驳回和上诉之后，终于走到了审判阶段。

sentences.en: David,
sentences.zh: 大卫，

sentences.en: I'm thinking kind of what would it mean if they make this big justice argument in front of this judge in this state that wrote the idea of a right to a clean environment into their constitution?
sentences.zh: 我在想，如果他们在这位法官面前提出这个宏大的正义论点，而这个州恰恰将清洁环境权的理念写进了宪法，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: What will that mean for this broader effort of looking for a solution to climate change through the courts?
sentences.zh: 这对于通过法院寻求气候变化解决方案这一更广泛的努力意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think it would call into question the effectiveness of this language that we're starting to see in more and more constitutions around the country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这会让人对我们在全国越来越多的宪法中开始看到的这种表述的有效性产生疑问。

sentences.en: And even more broadly than that,
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，

sentences.en: I think it would raise real questions about just how effective the courts can really be as part of the overall solution set to addressing the climate crisis right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会引发真正的疑问，即作为解决当前气候危机整体解决方案的一部分，法院究竟能发挥多大的实际效用。

sentences.en: That maybe courts aren't such a fruitful avenue for activists.
sentences.zh: 也许法院对活动人士来说并不是一个那么富有成效的途径。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We talk a lot about precedent and how cases can set precedent.
sentences.zh: 我们经常谈论先例以及案件如何树立先例。

sentences.en: And a defeat here would set a pretty troubling precedent for this legal strategy around the world.
sentences.zh: 这里的失败将为世界各地的这种法律战略树立一个相当令人不安的先例。

sentences.en: David, thank you.
sentences.zh: 大卫，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: All this week, the judge in Montana has been hearing testimony from the young activists as well as pediatricians and biologists.
sentences.zh: 整个这周，蒙大拿州的法官一直在听取年轻活动人士以及儿科医生和生物学家的证词。

sentences.en: Next week, the state is expected to mount its defense.
sentences.zh: 下周，预计该州将展开辩护。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的字谜游戏（Connections）。

sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.zh: 我是山姆·马苏尔斯基，我每天创作拼字蜜蜂（Spelling Bee）和 Letterboxd 游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到那些人一样。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Supreme Court handed a victory to Native American tribes, upholding a law aimed at keeping Native American children with their tribes and traditions.
sentences.zh: 周四，最高法院对美洲原住民部落作出了有利判决，维持了一项旨在让美洲原住民儿童留在其部落和传统的法律。

sentences.en: The case pitted a white couple from Texas against five tribes as they battled over the adoption of a Native American child.
sentences.zh: 该案让来自德克萨斯州的一对白人夫妇与五个部落展开对决，他们为争夺一名美洲原住民儿童的收养权而战。

sentences.en: The Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978 gives preference to Native families.
sentences.zh: 1978年的《印第安儿童福利法》给予原住民家庭优先权。

sentences.en: The couple argued that the act discriminated against non-Native families because it hinged on placement based on race.
sentences.zh: 这对夫妇辩称，该法案歧视非原住民家庭，因为它根据种族进行安置。

sentences.en: But the court ruled seven to two in favor of the tribes, upholding the law that was enacted to address the legacy of abuse of Native American children
sentences.zh: 但法院以七比二的投票结果支持了部落，维持了旨在解决美洲原住民儿童被虐待历史的法律，

sentences.en: who were being separated from their families and placed in non-Native homes.
sentences.zh: 这些儿童曾被迫与家人分离并被安置在非原住民家庭中。

sentences.en: And a federal grand jury has indicted Jack Teixeira, the 21-year-old Massachusetts Air National Guardsman,
sentences.zh: 联邦大陪审团已起诉21岁的马萨诸塞州空军国民警卫队员杰克·特谢拉，

sentences.en: who posted dozens of sensitive documents on social media on six counts of retaining and transmitting classified national defense information.
sentences.zh: 他在社交媒体上发布了数十份敏感文件，面临六项保留和传输国防机密信息的指控。

sentences.en: The indictment paves the way for a trial stemming from one of the most damaging national security leaks in recent history.
sentences.zh: 这份起诉书为审判铺平了道路，该审判源于近年最严重的国家安全泄密事件之一。

sentences.en: If convicted, he could face up to 60 years in prison.
sentences.zh: 如果罪名成立，他可能面临最高60年的监禁。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的技巧。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对黑暗敏感吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片了才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
